_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); semiconductor signals with NVIDIA's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (NVDA listed 1999-01-22)

pit_profile.why: 'NVIDIA is a visual computing company.' 'The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change, evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.' 'We expect substantial competition from both Intel's and AMD's, strategy of selling platform solutions, including integrating a CPU and a GPU on the same chip or same package, as evidenced by Intel's CPUs with integrated graphics and AMD's accelerated processing unit, or APU, products.' 'Our business is cyclical in nature and has experienced severe downturns that have harmed, and may in the future harm, our business and financial results.' (FY2014 10-K); CYCLICAL on the 10-K's own words for its business (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical' reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json covers a CPU and a GPU integrated on one chip, so those words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -17.8%/yr (worst year FY05-FY14 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +11.2%/yr (Q2 FY15 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY09 ex-FY10 median

BULL.desc: EPS +17.8%/yr (FY05-FY14 ex-FY09 ex-FY10 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +111.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY05-FY14 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NVDA (retrospective, 2014-05-30) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.50x (61.6% downside to Bear $7.30 / +40.9% upside to Bull $26.78) | Adj composite 2.47 vs market 2.24: gap +0.23 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | +83% above the EPP floor $10.36 (14x FY15E $0.74) | Conservative 2-yr case: -3.4% total (-1.7%/yr) | At 25.7x FY15E the 15% hurdle price $25.13 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +15.5% YoY in Q1 FY15, forward revenues +10.3-14.8% (Q2 FY15 revenue guide (Q1 FY15 release of May 8)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
